title: tuf-based-rotation-and-release-bundle-orchestration-for-private-installer-ci
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: private-installer releases need reproducible, auditable bundle indices and the ability to rotate signed metadata without causing client churn. This PR introduces a TUF-inspired rotation step in the CI build pipeline and a release-bundle orchestrator that assembles, signs, and publishes deltas and full bundles for VPC/on-prem installers.

What this changes: adds a new pipeline stage (bundle-orchestrator) that: 1) collects artifacts from build stages (helm charts, terraform modules, installer images), 2) generates a versioned release-bundle manifest, 3) publishes a TUF-style metadata tree and timestamp file, 4) rotates signing keys via cosign/HSM hooks, and 5) publishes a signed index and per-arch delta packages for faster upgrades. The orchestrator is configurable by env and supports dry-run, fast-forward-only, and emergency-rollback modes.

Key design notes: we adopted a minimal TUF-like metadata structure (root, targets, snapshot, timestamp) to avoid introducing a full TUF dependency in the installer; metadata is canonical JSON with deterministic sorting. Signing is pluggable: by default the pipeline uses cosign with keyless ephemeral annotations for PRs and KMS-backed keys for release branches. A lightweight provenance record (SBOM link + build-info) is attached to each target entry.

Checklist/QA: - [x] unit tests for metadata canonicalization - [x] integration tests for cosign sign/verify using test KMS - [x] e2e pipeline run on staging publishing a full bundle and delta - [x] upgrade test from 1.8.x -> 1.9.x using delta packages - [x] rollback test using timestamp truncation

Rollout plan: land to main behind feature flag CI_BUNDLE_ORCHESTRATOR=enabled. Run 3 weekly canary releases to staging, monitor installer clients for metadata fetch and verify latencies. After stable canaries, enable on release branch and perform signed release.

Rollback plan: orchestrator publishes incremental timestamped manifests. To roll back, operator may set ORCHESTRATOR_ROLLBACK_TO=<timestamp> which truncates timestamp and snapshot to a previous signed state; the pipeline validates metadata chain before publishing. In emergency the service supports publishing an emergency root rotation with operator approval.

Related: ENG-4128 (bundle rotation), ENG-4187 (installer upgrade reliability), SUP-1223 (customer report: failed private upgrades), docs PR will follow to document operator commands and KMS setup.

review_comments: Ben Carlson: Can we gate the root rotation behind the KMS approval flow? I want explicit operator ack before publishing. Author: added ORCHESTRATOR_FORCE_ROOT_ROTATION env and added audit log entry; kept manual switch for release branches.
Isabel Wu: The canonicalization needs deterministic ordering across go versions. Are we pinning encoding? Author: using go-jsoncanonical (vendor) and added tests across 1.19/1.20 CI matrix.

Diego Marquez: Delta publishing looks good but add verification step on consumer side; otherwise a corrupt delta could break upgrades. Author: added post-publish verification job and consumer verify script to charts.
CI Bot: pipeline passed on staging run #42 with cosign signatures validated.
Security Reviewer: confirm cosign key rotation docs and KMS IAM policy samples added. Author: pushed docs/operator/release-orchestrator.md and samples/iam-policy.json in a follow-up commit.
release_notes: Adds a TUF-style metadata orchestration stage to the private-installer CI that enables signed bundle rotation, delta publishing for faster upgrades, and operator-controlled rollback. Defaults to disabled; operators must enable via CI_BUNDLE_ORCHESTRATOR. See docs/operator/release-orchestrator.md for setup and KMS guidance.
merge_notes: Squash-merged after 2 approvals. Staging canary run successful; no regressions observed in installer metadata fetch paths.
post_merge_tasks: create docs PR to expand KMS examples and RBAC
announce in #release-automation and schedule operator training
add telemetry for metadata fetch latencies and cosign verification failures
notes: This PR intentionally avoids pulling in the full TUF Go library to keep the installer's runtime footprint small; we implement a compatible metadata layout sufficient for index rotation and verification. Future follow-ups may migrate to a full TUF implementation if needed.
